title: compatibility-extractor-and-phased-sunset-for-chatsocket
creator: Priya Nair
description: PRD: Provide a clear, low-risk migration path for customers using the legacy ChatSocket transport and legacy model aliasing behavior. Instead of an abrupt endpoint cutover, this initiative extracts a compatibility layer (the 'compatibility-extractor') that translates ChatSocket contracts into the new Unified Async transport and normalized model aliases. The extractor will run as a short-lived proxy (hosted by Redwood) and a customer-hosted adapter option for Dedicated/Private customers. Goals: minimize client breakage, preserve telemetry for rollback criteria, reduce server-side complexity over the medium term, and provide deterministic acceptance criteria for turning off the adapter. This doc defines scope, success metrics, rollout phases, monitoring gates, SDK/docs changes, and operational playbooks.
scope: Design and deliver a hosted compatibility-extractor service that accepts legacy ChatSocket connections and emits Unified Async requests with normalized model aliases.
Ship a client guidance kit with sample adapters (Node, Python) and a migration checklist for product/enterprise customers.
Define telemetry gates and automated rollback criteria tied to error rates, latency regressions, and model output divergence on a curated prompt set.
Create a customer opt-in window, shadowing mode, and an opt-out path for Dedicated/Private customers during initial rollout.
Coordinate SDK deprecations and add compatibility flags to Redwood JS/Python SDKs to help detect legacy usage patterns.
Operational runbook for scaling the extractor, rate limiting, and emergency fail-open policies.
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of customer client applications — we provide adapters and patterns but will not custom-migrate customers.
Changes to underlying model training or alias semantics beyond normalization mapping rules.
Permanent hosting of customer-specific adapters for Dedicated on-prem deployments (we'll provide tooling and templates).
migration_steps: Phase 0: Discovery — inventory active ChatSocket clients via telemetry and billing (completed: 2026-02-20).
Phase 1: Compatibility Extractor Alpha — internal testing with 3 pilot customers; implement alias normalization table and basic rate limiting (ETA: 2026-03-20).
Phase 2: Public Beta & SDK Flags — enable hosted extractor opt-in, ship SDK compatibility flag to surface deprecation warnings (ETA: 2026-04-05).
Phase 3: Shadow Mode — route 10% production traffic through extractor with no behavioral mutation, collect divergence metrics (ETA: 2026-04-18).
Phase 4: Gradual Redirect — offer customers a staged redirect with customer consent; monitor SLOs and customer reports (ETA: 2026-04-25).
Phase 5: Decommission Eligibility & Turnoff — after meeting gate criteria for 90 days and no P1 regressions, schedule extractor shutdown window (target: 2026-06-01).
rollout_timeline: 2026-02-10: PRD approved by PM and Eng leads.
2026-03-01 - 2026-03-20: Alpha pilots and internal load testing.
2026-04-05: Beta and SDK release with compatibility flag and migration guide.
2026-04-18: Begin shadowing and divergence evaluations (4 weeks).
2026-04-25 - 2026-05-25: Staged redirects for consenting customers and escalation cadence.
2026-06-01: Target earliest eligible turnoff date for extractor (subject to gate checks).
acceptance_criteria: Extractor correctly transforms 99.5% of observed ChatSocket request patterns in the pilot suite without semantic regression on the curated prompt set.
No P1 customer-facing regressions attributable to the extractor during 30 days of beta redirects (measured by error budget and escalations).
SDK telemetry flags detect and report 95% of legacy client usage patterns within 24 hours of activation.
Performance: 95th percentile additional latency introduced by extractor <= 35ms under expected load for production pilot cohort.
Operational: autoscaling policy validated such that CPU/GPU saturation events not caused by extractor in 99% of synthetic load tests.
Rollout gates: divergence score below threshold T (defined in 'monitoring' entry) for 28 consecutive days before scheduling shutdown.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Divergence metric: normalized embedding distance and generation token-level BLEU/ROUGE-like signals against curated prompt set (dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/compat-extractor-divergence).
Traffic classification: percentage of incoming ChatSocket requests using legacy model aliases (metric: legacy_alias_pct).
Error budget tracking: extractor-induced 5xxs and 4xxs by customer (alert threshold: 0.5% increase over baseline).
Latency breakdown: prefix parsing, alias normalization, network hop; visible per-route in Console tracing.
Customer support signals: automated tag on incoming incidents referencing ChatSocket adapter; escalate to PM/SE on P0/P1.
docs_and_sdk_changes: Python adapter template and Helm chart for Dedicated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/chatsocket-adapter-py
SDK changes: add 'legacyWarning' flag in JS/Python SDKs and runtime telemetry hook to emit 'legacy_client_detected'.
Support playbook: canned messages, FAQ, and rollback steps for Customer Success engineers.
open_questions: Billing model for hosted extractor during beta — should we bill zero, discounted, or metered? (action: Finance input required).
Customer-hosted adapter support SLA expectations for Dedicated customers — what qualifies as 'supported' vs 'best-effort'?
Edge cases: how to handle custom third-party proxies that inject headers or modify payloads (needs deeper packet examples from SEs).
Normalization rules: should we preserve deprecated alias synonyms or canonicalize strictly (trade-off: compatibility vs long-term alias sprawl).
